items.headline: Publishers file lawsuit against Google for AI training
items.excerpt: Major publishers including Hachette, Cengage and Elsevier sued Google, alleging it used digital copies from Google Books, Google Play and Google Scholar to train its Gemini model without permission. The complaint claims Google internally flagged the practice as 'highly problematic' and warned of billions in potential fines yet proceeded anyway. A rights/consent story shaping whether and how book text feeds AI models.

items.headline: Library News Round-Up, July 2026 (incl. ElevenLabs' AI-narrated Odyssey)
items.excerpt: Book Riot's July library round-up highlights ElevenLabs releasing an officially licensed AI-narrated edition of The Odyssey using a synthetic Michael Caine voice, alongside broader reading-crisis coverage. The item captures the arrival of licensed synthetic-voice narration in the commercial audiobook market and the job-displacement questions it raises for human narrators. A creative-AI capability landing in mainstream publishing.

items.headline: Court grants final approval to landmark $1.5 billion Anthropic settlement
items.excerpt: A federal judge granted final approval to the $1.5 billion Bartz v. Anthropic copyright settlement, with nearly 500,000 eligible works registered and authors set to receive up to about $3,000 per work while larger publishers gain tens of millions. The ruling establishes a concrete payout precedent for using copyrighted books to train large language models. Landmark rights outcome for the AI-and-books landscape.
